headline: Flyers activate Rasmus Ristolainen off injured reserve
take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Flyers have activated defenseman Rasmus Ristolainen off injured reserve, noting that Philadelphia is the only team in the Eastern Conference with a goal differential worse than -10.

The numbers back up the concern. PHI is 3-6-3 and has taken only 40.7% of the expected goals so far this season (expected goals measure the quality of chances, so that's a team being outplayed on shot quality). Five-on-five, the share drops to 37%. Ristolainen's return is modest help at best: in three games so far this season, the Flyers' five-on-five expected goal share was 5.6 points better when he was off the ice, and his own five-on-five share sat at 32.34%. His one goal is worth more than the 0.32 expected goals his chances were worth, so his production is running ahead of his play. He did play 18.28 minutes a night in that stretch.

Ristolainen's absence shifted the load. In the 5 games since he went out, Oliver Bonk has moved in beside Travis Sanheim, Nick Seeler is up to 21:09 a night from 17:35 and Sanheim is up to 27:28 from 24:22. Expect those minutes to ease as Ristolainen returns.
